transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I really don't want to make a big fuss out of nothing. But... I guess I came in because I just can’t seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, but at work—I'm a loan officer—I'll just sit and stare at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list, and I just end up rereading the same line over and over again. And then I'll put off making my calls because... well, even simple decisions just feel so much harder than they should lately. I'm sure it's probably just a normal phase, but does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you can help me with?
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Well, I really try to keep a positive attitude, I promise I do. But... I suppose if I'm being completely honest, most days there’s just this... this dull heaviness sitting with me. I don't want to sound ungrateful, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for, but even when I’m at the community center or out in my garden—places that always used to lift me right up—I kind of feel like I’m just going through the motions lately. 

I just keep a smile pasted on so I don't bother anyone else or bring them down. I hope that's not a terrible thing to admit. Does that sound like the sort of thing you were asking about?
Have you experienced any loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest at all. I still care very much about my garden and the community center. I'm out there every weekend, pulling weeds and helping out—I'd never want to just give up on the things I love, or let anyone down, you know? 

I promise I still really want to do them. It's really just... well, like I said, that heavy feeling just sort of tags along with me while I'm out there. But the interest itself is definitely still there. I hope I'm explaining the difference okay... does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, I... I know I probably should have come in sooner, and I'm really sorry if I let it go on too long. I kept thinking I could just push through it on my own, you know? 

But, um, I guess it's really been... a little over two years now. My, um, my close friend passed away back then, and... well, I suppose that dull feeling kind of started around then and just never quite lifted. I know grief takes time, and I really have been trying my best to move past it, I promise. I hope it's okay that I waited this long to ask for help... is two years a really long time to feel like this?
Do you still get pleasure from the activities you're doing, like gardening and helping out at the community center?

Oh, gosh, I'm... I'm not entirely sure how to answer that, I'm sorry. I hope I'm not being difficult. I guess I haven't really stopped to think about whether I'm feeling pleasure, exactly. 

I mean, I definitely still like being there, and I'm always glad to be of use to people. I'd hate to sound ungrateful or like I'm complaining! I just... I suppose I haven't really noticed that warm, happy spark I used to get from it. I mostly just focus on making sure I'm doing a good job and being helpful to everyone else, whether I'm at the center or at work. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question all right.
Do you feel like you're enjoying things less than you used to, even if you're still interested in them?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm not giving you very clear answers today. I hope I'm not making your job difficult. 

I honestly don't know for sure. I guess I just haven't really sat down and compared how much I enjoy things now versus a few years ago. I'd really hate to say I'm enjoying things *less*, because that sounds so negative and unappreciative, and I truly am grateful for my life. I still smile and feel good when I can help one of my credit counseling clients figure out their loans, or when the community garden looks nice. 

So, I'm just not entirely sure if the actual enjoyment is less, or if I'm just... well, maybe paying less attention to my own feelings while I'm doing those things. I hope that's an okay answer... I'm really trying my best to give you what you need!
Do you feel like you've lost the ability to feel happy or pleased, even when good things happen?

Oh, my, no... I really wouldn't say I've lost the ability completely. I'd feel terrible if I gave you that impression! 

I definitely still feel pleased when good things happen. Like, um, when I help one of my clients finally get their credit sorted out and they're just so relieved... I genuinely feel very happy for them. I might not be, you know, jumping up and down with excitement, but the happiness is absolutely still in there, I promise. 

I really don't want you to think I'm completely miserable or ignoring all the blessings in my life. I always try to look on the bright side when I can. Is it okay that I still have those good moments? I just hope I'm not making things too confusing for you by saying that.
Have you been experiencing any changes in your appetite or sleep patterns lately?

Oh, gosh... I hope I'm not being a bother by saying this, but I haven't really noticed any big changes. I mean, I sleep just fine, mostly. I might wake up a little early sometimes, but I think that's just getting older, you know? I wouldn't want to make a fuss over something normal. 

And my appetite is... well, it's pretty much the same. I still eat my regular meals. I always try to make sure I'm taking care of myself so I can keep up with work and the center. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you very exciting answers!
Have you been having any thoughts of death or suicide?

Oh, my goodness, no. No, absolutely not. Oh, dear... I hope I haven't said anything today that made you worry I might do something like that! I am so sorry if I gave you that dreadful impression. 

I would never... I mean, I know things feel a bit heavy for me sometimes, but I have so much to be grateful for. And my clients at the credit center really rely on me to help them sort out their loans. It would be just awful of me to even think about leaving them in a lurch, you know? I really just want to keep doing my best and being helpful to the people around me. 

I hope it's a relief to hear that? I promise you don't need to worry about me in that way. I'm just trying to keep putting one foot in front of the other and do the right thing.
Do you feel like your daily life has been significantly impacted by these feelings of heaviness and difficulty making decisions?

Well, um... I really try not to let it affect things too much. I mean, I always want to do a good job, you know? But... oh dear, I suppose if I'm being completely honest, I have been, well, postponing some of my client follow-ups at the credit office lately. Just a little bit! I always get to them eventually, I promise. It just takes me a bit longer to feel up to making the calls. I hope you don't think I'm being irresponsible.

And, um, I guess I have stepped back just a tiny bit from my usual activities. Like the gallery events I used to go to, and the walking-club outings... I used to make such a point of attending them. But lately, I just haven't had the energy to keep up with it all. I feel terrible about it, really. I don't want to let anyone down or seem anti-social. Is it understandable that I might need to take a little step back right now? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Would you say that these feelings of heaviness and difficulty making decisions are mild, or are they significantly interfering with your daily life?

Oh, goodness... um, I'm not entirely sure how to label it, to be perfectly honest. I really wouldn't want to use a strong phrase like "significantly interfering." That sounds so... well, so dramatic, doesn't it? And I really do try my hardest to keep things running smoothly. I'm still going to the credit office, and I'm still taking care of my responsibilities, even if I'm a little slow with the phone calls. 

It's just... maybe it's a little more than mild? Just because it takes so much extra effort lately to push through that heavy feeling. But I'm still managing! I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up or letting everything fall apart, because I'm absolutely not. I hope I'm explaining that right? I just wouldn't want to make a mountain out of a molehill if this is just a normal rough patch that people go through.
Would you say that these feelings are affecting your ability to function at work or in your daily activities more than 50% of the time?

Oh, 50 percent... that sounds like such a high number, doesn't it? I really hate to think I'm dropping the ball quite that often. But... well, like I was saying just a moment ago about putting off my client follow-ups at the credit office, and staying home from the gallery events and the walking-club outings... I suppose if I'm being completely honest with you, and if I really count up the days where I just can't quite manage to do those things... it might actually be right around half the time. Maybe just a little over? 

I do try my absolute best to push through, though, I promise you that. Do you think that makes me sound terribly unreliable? I really am trying to keep up with everything as best I can, I just hope I'm not doing a terrible job of it.
Would you say that most days are affected by this heavy feeling and difficulty making decisions, or is it more intermittent?

Oh, most days... yes, I suppose it is most days. I really wish I could say it was just every now and then, I truly do. But... well, if I'm being honest, there's just this dull heaviness sitting with me almost all the time lately. 

I try so hard not to let it show! Even when I go down to the community center, or when I'm out tending to my garden—and those are things that always used to just lift my spirits right up—I find myself just... going through the motions. I make sure to keep a smile pasted on, of course, because I'd hate to bring anyone else down or make them worry about me. I hope that's the right way to handle it? I just want to be a pleasant presence for people, even if I'm feeling a bit weighed down inside. Does that make sense?
Would you say that these feelings of heaviness and difficulty making decisions are causing you significant distress or impairment in your daily life?

Oh, "significant distress"... that sounds so serious, doesn't it? I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or making a fuss. I mean, I'm still getting out of bed and putting my clothes on every day, so I'm not completely falling apart or anything! 

But... well, I suppose if I'm looking at it honestly... it is getting a bit harder to keep all the plates spinning. Like I mentioned before, I've started putting off my client follow-ups at the credit office. I just... I look at the files and I can't seem to make the decisions I need to make, so I push them to the next day. And I've pretty much stopped going to the gallery events, and I haven't been to the walking-club outings in... oh, a while now. I used to make such a point of attending those, but lately it just feels like too much effort to be sociable and pretend everything is fine. 

I feel terrible about it, honestly. I hate letting my clients down, and I worry my friends at the club think I'm ignoring them. I do try to catch up when I have a good day, I really do. I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy or giving up on things? I'm trying my best to manage it all, I just... I suppose it is getting in the way more than I'd like to admit. Is it normal to struggle this much with things that used to be so easy?
Would you say that these feelings are making it hard for you to do even the smallest tasks most of the time?

Oh, the smallest tasks... well, I wouldn't say it's *hard* to do them, exactly. I can still do them! I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing all day. 

But... oh, it's just that I feel so very tired lately. I really try to get a good night's sleep, I make sure I'm in bed at a reasonable hour, but I still wake up feeling just as exhausted as when I went to sleep. And then... well, by the time I've managed to get through just a couple of client calls for work, or even just gone out to water my tomatoes—which usually doesn't take long at all—my whole body just feels so heavy. It feels like I've already worked a full eight-hour day, even though it's only mid-morning. 

I feel so silly even mentioning it, because watering tomatoes is hardly hard labor, is it? I really do push myself to keep going, though. I don't want to be someone who just gives up because they're a little tired. Do you think it's alright that I need to rest so much more often now? I just hope I'm not making too big a deal out of being a bit fatigued.
Would you say that these feelings are impacting your ability to take care of your basic needs, like eating or showering?

Oh, my basic needs? Oh goodness, no, I wouldn't say it's gotten that bad! I really do make sure to keep up with all of that. I'd be so embarrassed if I let myself go, you know? 

I still shower every morning, just like always, and I make sure my clothes are neat and tidy for work, even if I'm just working from my desk at home. And I'm definitely still eating! I try to make sure I have a proper breakfast and lunch, even if it's just something small. I don't want to cause any worry by skipping meals or anything like that. 

I mean, maybe I don't cook those big, elaborate dinners like I used to—sometimes I just pop a frozen meal in the oven because I'm so worn out by the evening—but I'm certainly not starving myself or neglecting my hygiene. I think I'm doing an okay job keeping up with the essentials, don't you? I really try to be responsible about those things, even when I'm feeling a bit down. I hope that's what you were asking?
Would you say that your feelings of heaviness and difficulty making decisions are more of a mild annoyance or a major obstacle in your daily life?

Oh, "major obstacle"... that sounds so dramatic, doesn't it? I really wouldn't want to use a word like that. It makes it sound like I'm just completely failing at everything, and I promise I'm not! I'm still trying very hard to keep up.

But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest, it is a bit more than just a mild annoyance. Like I might have mentioned before, I have started postponing my client follow-ups at the credit office. I just... I look at the files and I can't quite make the decisions I need to, so I push them off. And I've stepped back from the gallery events and the walking-club outings that I always used to make a point of attending. 

I feel so guilty about it, I really do. I don't want my clients or my friends to think I'm unreliable or that I don't care. I just... I run out of steam, and deciding what to do just feels so heavy. I hope you don't think I'm just making excuses? I really am trying my best to push through it. Do you think it's understandable that I'm struggling with these things a little bit right now?
Would you say that your feelings of heaviness are present nearly every day?

Oh, nearly every day? Well... I suppose so, yes. But I don't want it to sound like I'm just miserable all the time! I really do try to keep a positive attitude. 

It's just... most days, there's this sort of... dull heaviness that just sits with me. I still get out and do things, I promise! I still go to the community center, and I'm out in my garden. Those places used to really lift my spirits, but lately... well, it feels a bit like I'm just going through the motions. I make sure to keep a smile pasted on, of course, because I'd hate to bring anyone else down. I don't want people to worry about me when they have their own lives to manage. 

Do you think it's normal to feel that way even when you're doing things you're supposed to enjoy? I just hope I'm not complaining too much about something that's just a normal part of getting older.
Would you say that your feelings of heaviness and difficulty making decisions are interfering with your daily life to a degree that you would consider moderate, rather than mild?

Oh, moderate... well, I suppose that might be a fair word for it, if you think so. I really hate to make a fuss, but... yes, I think I'd have to agree it's a bit more than mild. 

Like I was saying earlier, it's just getting harder to keep all the plates spinning. I've been putting off those client follow-ups at the credit office, which isn't like me at all. I just look at the paperwork and feel so overwhelmed, so I set it aside. And I haven't been going to the gallery events or the walking-club outings either. I used to never miss those! I always made such a point to be involved. 

I just feel terrible about it. I don't want to let anyone down or seem like I'm slacking off. I really am trying to keep up with everything, I promise. Do you think it's alright that I'm stepping back just a little bit right now? I just hope I'm not making too much out of it.
Would you say that your feelings of heaviness and difficulty making decisions are significantly interfering with your ability to function in your daily life?

Oh, "significantly"... well, I know I keep saying the exact same things, and I am so sorry if I sound like a broken record! I really don't want you to think I'm completely falling apart, because I promise I'm still trying my very best to hold everything together. 

But... yes, I suppose it is interfering a fair bit. Just like I mentioned before, I've started postponing my client follow-ups at the credit office. I just can't seem to tackle them right now. And I really have stepped back from the gallery events and the walking-club outings that I always used to make such a point of attending. 

I feel just awful admitting that out loud again. I really should be able to handle my normal routine better than this, shouldn't I? I hope you don't judge me too harshly for letting things slide a little bit lately. I really am trying to get back on track.
